In the triangle above, what is the length of $\overset{―}{AC}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's refer to our standard ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14165760/assets/85f119cdc6b7a80dd7cd4ea2a2a235e80723b7c2fe6837fa127beb8fd994d7ea.png)

Since this is a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle, the length of the longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times that of the shorter leg.

Here, the shorter leg has length $x=2\sqrt{3}$ and the longer leg has length $\sqrt{3}x,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}AC=\sqrt{3}x=\sqrt{3}\cdot 2\sqrt{3}=3\cdot 2=6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the length of the longer leg is $6.$
